sentence_stem: Her phone has been switched off all day, so
correct_completion: she must have forgotten to charge it.
full_sentence: Her phone has been switched off all day, so she must have forgotten to charge it.
acceptable_variants: she might have run out of battery.
she must have left it at home.

options.text: she has been talking on the phone all day.
options.why_wrong: This contradicts the stem: a phone that is switched off cannot be used for calls.

options.text: she will have finished her homework by tonight.
options.why_wrong: This describes a future completion and does not explain why the phone is switched off.

options.text: she must have forgotten to charge it.
she should buy a new phone immediately.
options.why_wrong: This gives advice rather than a logical deduction about the past reason for the phone being off.

grammar_focus: Modal perfect of deduction: must have + past participle
explanation: The modal 'must have' with a past participle expresses a logical conclusion about a past event, based on evidence in the present. Learners whose first language expresses inferred past through a different grammatical system often choose a simple past or a plain future form here, so the modal perfect needs focused practice.
translation: Telefonu bütün gün kapalıydı, bu yüzden şarjı takmayı unutmuş olmalı.
